cells.text: You are asking someone to buy something they cannot stand in

Real estate in Saudi Arabia is understood physically. You see the building, you hold the deed, you know the street. Fractional ownership breaks all three: you buy 1% of a property you will never visit, through an app, and what you own is a certificate rather than a door.
Everything else about the product was secondary to that. The listings, the returns, the payment flow: none of it matters if the person does not first believe that what they are buying is real.
Three constraints, and none of them optional

items: Sharia compliance. The investment structure had to be reviewed and approved by a scholar, and that approval had to be visible in the product, not filed away.
Regulatory. Hissatech operates inside the Saudi Real Estate General Authority (REGA) regulatory sandbox, which governs what can be claimed and how.
Arabic and RTL. Not a translation layer. The product is Arabic first, and the layout, numerals, and reading order follow from that.

cells.text: Most product constraints are trade-offs you can argue about. These three were fixed before design started, and the work was to make them read as reassurance rather than as fine print.
Show the arithmetic, do not explain the concept
The instinct with an unfamiliar financial product is to explain it. We did the opposite and showed the sum, in the plainest numbers we could find:

rows: You own 1% of the property, and 1% of its rent

cells.text: One worked example does what three paragraphs of definition cannot. A reader who follows that division has understood fractional ownership without ever being taught the term.

cells.caption: Explain why this matters — not what it is.
